issues.description: The differential run shows the golden/expert submission fails SR1 with 'trigger_scenario names both branch registers with no primary target distinguished, inconsistent with vulnerable_register=sig_q_reg'. This means the golden solution is rejected by the grader (golden_rejected failure class), directly contradicting the requirement that a correct submission must pass. The primary-register determination logic in trigger_scenario evidently mismatches vulnerable_register's determined primary (sig_q_reg vs expected sig_p_reg per fixture), or the golden trigger_scenario text triggers the ambiguous-both-registers path in determine_primary_register for that field even when vulnerable_register itself is unambiguous.
issues.evidence: golden_run.stdout: '[TEST] FAIL: SR1: trigger_scenario names both branch registers with no primary target distinguished, inconsistent with vulnerable_register=sig_q_reg' while golden_run.expected='pass' and exit_code=1

issues.description: The regression self-check for determine_primary_register only validates the vulnerable_register-style fixture (golden_fixture.json), not the corresponding trigger_scenario parsing path. Since SR1's failure originates from trigger_scenario's primary-register determination (or its fallback single-token matching) disagreeing with vulnerable_register's determination, the fixture/regression test provides false confidence that the primary-register logic is safe, when in fact an equivalent bug exists on the trigger_scenario side.
issues.evidence: golden_fixture.json only encodes an 'expected_primary_register' for the vulnerable_register field; no analogous fixture/test exists for trigger_scenario text, yet the actual golden-run failure occurs when comparing trig_primary (or its ambiguous detection) against vr_primary.

issues.description: Mutation scoring is blocked entirely because the differential check failed at the golden-acceptance stage, so mutation_score_meaningful=false and requirement_discrimination_coverage_score=0.0 — none of the FR/SR checks have been validated against actual mutants, leaving the benchmark's discriminative power completely unverified.

recommendations: Fix determine_primary_register's application to trigger_scenario so that the golden solution's trigger_scenario field (naming a single primary fault register, likely sig_p_reg or sig_q_reg consistently with vulnerable_register) is not misclassified as 'both registers asserted with no primary' — inspect why trig_primary/trig_ambiguous diverges from vr_primary for the actual golden vulnerability_report.json content.

Add a golden_fixture-style regression test for trigger_scenario parsing analogous to the existing one for vulnerable_register, so that both fields' primary-register determination logic are jointly regression-tested against realistic golden-style prose (e.g., prose that mentions both registers when explaining the recombination formula uses both sig_p_reg and sig_q_reg, which is very plausible in a real trigger_scenario description of forcing one register while the other is also referenced as unaffected).

Inspect and correct the actual golden/vulnerability_report.json content or the SR1 matching logic in evaluate.py so the expert solution passes end-to-end (differential status must be 'pass', not 'fail') before this benchmark case can be considered usable.
Re-run the differential and mutation analysis after the SR1 fix to confirm mutation_score_meaningful becomes true and discrimination coverage is validated across FR1-FR4/SR1-SR4.
